body:
Coordinator review of the unpublished first #1251 implementation found an overrestrictive condition before final independent review: `final_families == prior_families`, followed by unchanged-key requirements for every member of every prior family. This rejects supported corrections that remove a collision, including the reviewed generic Peptone change away from MICRO:0000178, even though no new colliding pair is introduced. The original guard allowed owners to leave a family. This draft regression must not cause those supported changes to be deferred.

The precise constraint is no new colliding path pairs across the complete before/after catalog. Every surviving inherited collision must keep its same paths, keys and statuses under the bounded exception; a source owner that leaves the family without a new collision remains subject to the ordinary full provenance, preimage, identity-review and schema checks. Decreasing a two- or three-member family is not a new collision. Constant-size replacement, a new third member, renamed/reidentified surviving collisions and tombstone revival must still fail.

Preserve the initial draft and diagnostic tests. Add positive reductions of two- and three-member families, alongside the existing actual nickel pair, unchanged rejected records, and meaningful negative controls. Do not split batches, select an identity winner, change source payloads or weaken any scientific acceptance guard. This is a correction to the new implementation, not an exception to identity semantics.

Captured draft SHA256: `7f6be1c3dd66838b487d7b8fbc08f23eed6117b26ee540612eff49dc888be511`. Evidence: `.temp/all-unmatched-20261107/preflight/native-family-reduction-finding-publication-v1/operator-draft.py`. Author was notified and paused this correction until this addendum. No maintained source application or commit has occurred. Final code still requires independent adversarial review and full test/CI validation.
